newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Monday with big institutions borrowing against early-maturing contracts to prepare for trading in new domestic A shares to be listed on the Shenzhen stock exchange shortly, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract rose to 5.99 percent from 3.0 percent last Friday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose sharply to 7.04 million lots from 2.68 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.

Traders said major institutions borrowed heavily on Monday for trading in new A shares in Shenzhen, and for further trading on both the Shanghai and Shenzhen A share markets, which have put in strong performances recently.

This triggered follow-up buying from other investors, pushing up Monday's rates and volume, they said, adding that they expected the repo contracts to continue to rise in the next few days due to strong fundamentals on the A share markets.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Monday on a technical correction after successive rises in the past few trading days, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell to 117.85 yuan from 118.17 yuan.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market fell to 2.36 million lots from 2.57 million lots.
"Profit-taking set in today after successive gains in the past few trading days," one trader said. "But sentiment remains strong and the market will recover soon from the correction."
The market strength has come from recent talk that the central bank would possibly cut bank interest rates and lower coupon rates for the latest batch issued from March 1.
